words.enDefinition: feeling very tense and unable to relax because of pressure

examples.en: I've been so stressed out about finals that I can't sleep properly.
examples.zh: 期末临近，我一直「压力很大」，觉都睡不好。

examples.en: My roommate gets stressed out every time she checks her budget.
examples.zh: 每次一查自己的预算，室友就「压力山大」。

words.enDefinition: annoyed beyond patience and wanting a situation to stop

examples.en: I'm fed up with my roommate leaving dirty dishes in the sink.
examples.zh: 我真是「受够了」室友总把脏盘子留在水槽里。

examples.en: After three straight weeks of rain, the whole campus is fed up.
examples.zh: 连下了三个星期的雨，全校的人都「烦透了」。

words.enDefinition: mentally exhausted after a long period of stress or work

examples.en: After nonstop deadlines this month, I feel completely burned out.
examples.zh: 这个月截止日期接连不断，我感觉已经完全「身心俱疲」。

examples.en: She was so burned out from studying that she slept all weekend.
examples.zh: 她学习学得「心力交瘁」，整个周末都在睡觉。

words.enDefinition: extremely tired with no energy left at all

examples.en: I was completely exhausted after pulling two all-nighters in a row.
examples.zh: 连熬两个通宵之后，我已经「筋疲力尽」。

examples.en: She looked exhausted but kept studying until the library closed.
examples.zh: 她一脸「疲惫」，却还坚持学习到图书馆闭馆。

words.enDefinition: feeling that all your energy has been used up

examples.en: Back-to-back lectures leave me feeling totally drained by Friday afternoon.
examples.zh: 连轴转的课上下来，周五下午我已经觉得「精力耗尽」。

examples.en: Constant arguments with my roommate have left me emotionally drained.
examples.zh: 和室友不断的争执让我情绪上也被「耗尽」了。

words.enDefinition: feeling unable to deal with everything at once

examples.en: With five deadlines next week, I'm honestly feeling a bit overwhelmed.
examples.zh: 下周有五个截止日期，说实话我有点「不堪重负」。

examples.en: Many new international students feel overwhelmed by the English paperwork.
examples.zh: 很多新留学生都被英文材料手续搞得「手足无措」。

words.enDefinition: worried or slightly afraid about something you must do

examples.en: I was so nervous before my first presentation in English.
examples.zh: 第一次用英语做展示前，我「紧张」得不行。

examples.en: Don't be nervous; the professor just wants to chat about your essay.
examples.zh: 别「紧张」，教授只是想聊聊你的论文。

words.enDefinition: unhappy because you keep thinking about a possible problem

examples.en: My mom gets worried whenever I don't reply to her messages.
examples.zh: 只要我不回消息，我妈就会很「担心」。

examples.en: Honestly, I'm a little worried about my grades this semester.
examples.zh: 说实话，我有点「担心」这学期的成绩。

words.enDefinition: slightly worried that something is wrong or unsafe

examples.en: I felt uneasy leaving my laptop unattended in the library.
examples.zh: 把笔记本电脑留在图书馆没人看，我心里很「不踏实」。

examples.en: Something about his tone made me uneasy during our group meeting.
examples.zh: 小组会议上，他说话的语气让我有点「不安」。

words.enDefinition: so nervous that your body or the atmosphere feels stiff

examples.en: The room went tense when the professor mentioned a surprise quiz.
examples.zh: 教授提到突击测验时，教室里的气氛一下子「紧绷」起来。

examples.en: My shoulders get tense after hours of staring at my thesis.
examples.zh: 盯着论文好几个小时后，我的肩膀都「绷紧」了。

words.enDefinition: unable to relax or stay still, often from worry or boredom

examples.en: I felt restless all evening, pacing around my dorm room.
examples.zh: 整个晚上我都「静不下来」，在宿舍里走来走去。

examples.en: The day before results come out, everyone gets restless in class.
examples.zh: 出成绩的前一天，课堂上大家都「坐立不安」。

words.enDefinition: nervous and easily irritated because you expect trouble

examples.en: Everyone has been on edge since the professor announced the final.
examples.zh: 自从教授宣布期末考试安排后，大家都「紧张不安」。

examples.en: Our loud neighbors keep me on edge almost every night.
examples.zh: 吵闹的邻居让我几乎每晚都「神经紧绷」。

words.enDefinition: annoyed because you cannot achieve or change what you want

examples.en: I get frustrated when I can't express my ideas in English.
examples.zh: 没法用英语表达自己的想法时，我会很「沮丧」。

examples.en: He sounded frustrated after failing the driving test a third time.
examples.zh: 驾照考试第三次没过，他听起来很「懊恼」。

words.enDefinition: to become very upset or agitated about something

examples.en: I tend to get worked up when I cannot find something before class.
examples.zh: 上课前找不到东西时，我容易「变得越来越激动」。

examples.en: My flatmate told me not to get worked up about one missed bus.
examples.zh: 室友劝我别为错过一班公交就「变得越来越激动」。

collocations: get worked up over a small mistake
try not to get worked up

words.enDefinition: sad and offended because someone treated you badly

examples.en: I felt hurt when none of my roommates invited me to dinner.
examples.zh: 室友们没一个叫我去吃晚饭，我感到很「受伤」。

examples.en: Her careless joke about my accent left me genuinely hurt.
examples.zh: 她随口拿我的口音开玩笑，让我真的很「受伤」。

words.enDefinition: feeling ashamed because you did something wrong

examples.en: I feel guilty for not calling my grandparents more often.
examples.zh: 很少给爷爷奶奶打电话，我心里很「内疚」。

examples.en: She felt guilty about eating my snacks without asking first.
examples.zh: 她没先问我就吃了我的零食，觉得挺「愧疚」的。

words.enDefinition: worried about how you look or sound to other people

examples.en: I felt self-conscious speaking English in front of native speakers.
examples.zh: 在母语者面前说英语，我很「在意别人的眼光」。

examples.en: She's self-conscious about her accent, so please don't tease her.
examples.zh: 她很「在意」自己的口音，请别拿这个打趣她。

words.enDefinition: uncomfortable and unsure how to behave in a social situation

examples.en: It was awkward running into my ex at the dining hall.
examples.zh: 在食堂撞见前任，场面特别「尴尬」。

examples.en: There was an awkward silence after someone mentioned the failed exam.
examples.zh: 有人提到挂科的事后，出现了一阵「尴尬的」沉默。

words.enDefinition: not confident about yourself or your own abilities

examples.en: Comparing myself to my classmates online always makes me feel insecure.
examples.zh: 总在网上和同学攀比，让我很「不自信」。

examples.en: He gets insecure whenever the professor critiques his writing in class.
examples.zh: 教授在课上点评他的写作时，他就变得「不自信」。

words.enDefinition: feeling less confident or enthusiastic after a setback

examples.en: I felt deflated when the event I had helped organize was cancelled.
examples.zh: 得知自己参与筹办的活动取消后，我「一下泄了气」。

examples.en: She looked deflated after finding out that the workshop had filled up.
examples.zh: 得知培训名额已满后，她看起来「一下泄了气」。

words.enDefinition: having lost your motivation to keep trying

examples.en: Don't get discouraged; everyone struggles with academic writing at first.
examples.zh: 别「灰心」，一开始人人都不适应学术写作。

examples.en: After failing the placement test twice, he felt pretty discouraged.
examples.zh: 分级考试两次都没过，他挺「泄气」的。

words.enDefinition: extremely sad and shocked, often by very bad news

examples.en: She was absolutely devastated when she saw her final grade online.
examples.zh: 在网上看到期末成绩时，她整个人都「崩溃了」。

examples.en: He was devastated by the rejection and skipped the club meeting.
examples.zh: 被拒之后他「备受打击」，连社团会议都没去。

words.enDefinition: extremely sad, as if your heart is broken

examples.en: He was heartbroken when his girlfriend broke up with him.
examples.zh: 女朋友和他分手时，他「心碎」不已。

examples.en: I was heartbroken to say goodbye to my friends back home.
examples.zh: 和家乡的朋友们道别时，我「伤心欲绝」。

words.enDefinition: very unhappy and uncomfortable for a long time

examples.en: I felt miserable during my first lonely week in the dorm.
examples.zh: 住进宿舍后第一个孤单的星期，我过得非常「难受」。

examples.en: The cold rainy weather made our camping trip absolutely miserable.
examples.zh: 又冷又雨的天气让我们的露营之旅「苦不堪言」。

words.enDefinition: sad and low in energy for a short while

examples.en: I've been feeling a bit down since my best friend moved away.
examples.zh: 自从最好的朋友搬走后，我一直有点「情绪低落」。

examples.en: Missing my mom's cooking always gets me down in winter.
examples.zh: 冬天吃不到妈妈做的菜，总让我「情绪低落」。

words.enDefinition: very sad and without energy or hope for a while

examples.en: He felt depressed for weeks after failing his driving test.
examples.zh: 驾照考试没过后，他「消沉」了好几个星期。

examples.en: The long gray winters here make some international students depressed.
examples.zh: 这里漫长阴沉的冬天让一些留学生「情绪低迷」。

words.enDefinition: feeling that nothing you do will improve the situation

examples.en: After the third internship rejection, I started to feel hopeless.
examples.zh: 第三次实习被拒后，我开始感到「无望」。

examples.en: Don't feel hopeless about your English; it improves every week.
examples.zh: 别觉得英语没「希望」了，它每周都在进步。

words.enDefinition: sad because you miss your home country and family

examples.en: I get homesick every time I smell food from my hometown.
examples.zh: 每次闻到家乡菜的味道，我都会「想家」。

examples.en: She felt really homesick during her first semester in Canada.
examples.zh: 在加拿大的第一学期，她特别「想家」。

words.enDefinition: sad because a group is doing something without you

examples.en: They kept switching to German, and I felt completely left out.
examples.zh: 他们老是用德语聊天，我觉得自己完全被「晾在一边」。

examples.en: Nobody invited her to the study group, so she felt left out.
examples.zh: 没人叫她加入学习小组，她感到被「排挤」了。

words.enDefinition: unable to feel anything because something has shocked you

examples.en: After hours of waiting, I just felt numb about the results.
examples.zh: 等了几个小时之后，我对结果已经感觉「麻木」了。

examples.en: I went numb when I read the rejection email this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上读到拒信时，我整个人都「麻了」。

words.enDefinition: easily moved to tears or strong feelings

examples.en: I get really emotional whenever I watch old graduation videos online.
examples.zh: 每次在网上看以前的毕业视频，我都会特别「动情」。

examples.en: Don't mind him; he's just emotional after the long flight.
examples.zh: 别介意他，他坐了长途飞机，有点「情绪化」。

words.enDefinition: feeling both happy and sad when remembering the past

examples.en: Scrolling through old high school photos made the whole group nostalgic.
examples.zh: 翻看高中老照片，让整个群里的人都「怀旧」起来。

examples.en: I always feel nostalgic when I hear songs from my hometown.
examples.zh: 每次听到家乡的歌，我都会很「怀旧」。

words.enDefinition: disgusted by something dirty or unpleasant, informal

examples.en: I was grossed out by the moldy leftovers in our shared fridge.
examples.zh: 公共冰箱里发霉的剩菜让我「恶心」坏了。

examples.en: My roommate got grossed out when the sink wouldn't drain.
examples.zh: 水池排水不畅时，室友「恶心」得直皱眉。

words.enDefinition: happy that something bad ended or did not happen

examples.en: I was so relieved when the professor postponed the quiz.
examples.zh: 教授推迟测验时，我「如释重负」。

examples.en: She felt deeply relieved after finally submitting her thesis draft.
examples.zh: 终于交上论文初稿后，她深感「松了一口气」。

words.enDefinition: expecting good things to happen in the future

examples.en: I'm feeling optimistic about finding a part-time job before September.
examples.zh: 我对九月前找到兼职这件事很「乐观」。

examples.en: She stayed optimistic even after failing her first job interview.
examples.zh: 第一次求职面试失败后，她依然很「乐观」。

words.enDefinition: extremely excited and pleased about something good

examples.en: I was thrilled to hear I got the research assistant position.
examples.zh: 听说拿到了研究助理的职位，我「激动」极了。

examples.en: She was thrilled when her favorite singer replied to her comment.
examples.zh: 喜欢的歌手回复了她的评论，她「乐坏了」。

words.enDefinition: very pleased about something that has happened

examples.en: I'm delighted that my host family invited me for Thanksgiving.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭邀请我一起过感恩节，我「高兴」极了。

examples.en: The professor said she was delighted with our group's presentation.
examples.zh: 教授说她对我们小组的展示「非常满意」。

words.enDefinition: very excited and full of energy for something, informal

examples.en: I'm so pumped for the basketball final against our rivals tonight!
examples.zh: 今晚和死对头打篮球决赛，我「热血沸腾」。

examples.en: Our intramural team was totally pumped after winning the championship.
examples.zh: 赢得校内联赛冠军后，我们队「士气高涨」。

words.enDefinition: having a strong reason or drive to work hard

examples.en: I feel really motivated now that I've set my semester goals.
examples.zh: 定好这学期的目标后，我「干劲十足」。

examples.en: Studying with her friends keeps her motivated before the finals.
examples.zh: 期末考前和朋友一起学习让她始终保持「有动力」。

words.enDefinition: calm and free from worry or tension

examples.en: I felt so relaxed after the hot spring trip with friends.
examples.zh: 和朋友们泡完温泉回来，我「放松」极了。

examples.en: She looked completely relaxed and confident during her thesis defense.
examples.zh: 答辩全程她都显得十分「放松」、自信。

words.enDefinition: not angry, excited, or worried

examples.en: Try to stay calm when the professor asks you a surprise question.
examples.zh: 教授突击提问时，尽量保持「冷静」。

examples.en: A ten-minute meditation helps me stay calm before big exams.
examples.zh: 考前做十分钟冥想能帮我保持「平静」。

words.enDefinition: very surprised by something bad or unexpected

examples.en: I was shocked to see my electricity bill this month.
examples.zh: 看到这个月的电费账单，我「惊呆」了。

examples.en: Everyone was shocked when the quiet guy won the talent show.
examples.zh: 那个安静的男生赢了才艺比赛，大家都「震惊」了。

words.enDefinition: extremely happy and pleased about something, informal

examples.en: She was over the moon when she won the essay competition.
examples.zh: 作文比赛获奖时，她「欣喜若狂」。

examples.en: Mom was over the moon when I told her I passed my exams.
examples.zh: 我告诉妈妈考试都通过时，她「乐开了花」。

words.enDefinition: the happy feeling when something bad ends or is avoided

examples.en: Finishing my last final brought instant relief and a long nap.
examples.zh: 考完最后一科，我顿时感到「如释重负」，补了个长觉。

examples.en: It was such a relief to hear my package wasn't lost.
examples.zh: 听说包裹没有丢，真是「如释重负」。

words.enDefinition: the annoyed feeling when things keep going wrong

examples.en: Learning to write essays in English is full of frustration.
examples.zh: 用英语学写论文的过程充满了「挫败感」。

examples.en: He closed his laptop in frustration after losing his entire essay.
examples.zh: 论文全丢了之后，他满怀「挫败感」地合上了电脑。

words.enDefinition: a strong worried feeling that something bad may happen

examples.en: During exam season, quiet anxiety fills every corner of the library.
examples.zh: 考试季，图书馆的每个角落都弥漫着「焦虑」。

examples.en: She manages her anxiety before presentations with slow, deep breathing.
examples.zh: 她用缓慢的深呼吸来缓解上台演讲前的「焦虑」。

words.enDefinition: a nervous, unfriendly feeling between people or in a place

examples.en: There was real tension in the room when the grades were posted.
examples.zh: 成绩一公布，教室里顿时充满了「紧张气氛」。

examples.en: Chores have created some tension between me and my roommate.
examples.zh: 家务分工让我和室友之间产生了些「紧张气氛」。

words.enDefinition: extreme tiredness caused by working too hard for too long

examples.en: Midterm burnout is real; our whole study group felt it.
examples.zh: 期中「倦怠」是真实存在的，我们整个学习小组都体会到了。

examples.en: Taking Sundays completely off helped me avoid burnout this semester.
examples.zh: 这学期周日彻底休息帮我避免了「身心透支」。

words.enDefinition: the feeling of being slightly angry about something

examples.en: To my annoyance, the printer broke right before my deadline.
examples.zh: 让我「恼火」的是，打印机偏偏在截止日前坏了。

examples.en: He couldn't hide his annoyance at the constant construction noise.
examples.zh: 施工噪音不断，他掩不住一脸「烦躁」。

words.enDefinition: an angry, bitter feeling after being treated unfairly

examples.en: Quiet resentment built up as I always cleaned the shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 公共厨房总是我在打扫，「怨气」慢慢积了起来。

examples.en: She hid her resentment when her teammate took all the credit.
examples.zh: 队友抢走了全部功劳，她把「不满」埋在心里。

words.enDefinition: the unhappy feeling when someone else has what you want

examples.en: A little jealousy is normal when your best friend studies abroad.
examples.zh: 好友出国留学时，心里有点「嫉妒」很正常。

examples.en: His jealousy disappeared once he made his own friends here.
examples.zh: 他在这里交到自己的朋友后，「嫉妒」就消失了。

words.enDefinition: the unhappy feeling that you have done something wrong

examples.en: I felt real guilt after yelling at my little brother on the phone.
examples.zh: 在电话里冲弟弟吼了之后，我满是「内疚」。

examples.en: She skipped the party out of guilt about her unfinished homework.
examples.zh: 因为作业没做完的「愧疚」，她没去参加聚会。

words.enDefinition: the shy, uncomfortable feeling you have in front of others

examples.en: My face turned red with embarrassment when I forgot her name.
examples.zh: 忘了她的名字时，我「尴尬」得满脸通红。

examples.en: To everyone's embarrassment, the microphone stopped working during the speech.
examples.zh: 让大家「尴尬」的是，演讲中途麦克风没声了。

words.enDefinition: doubts about a decision already made or about to be made

examples.en: I had second thoughts about taking the early shift after seeing my timetable.
examples.zh: 看到课表后，我对接早班「又有些犹豫」。

examples.en: My roommate expressed second thoughts after we saw how far away the flat was.
examples.zh: 发现那套公寓离得太远后，室友说自己「又有些犹豫」。

collocations: have second thoughts about a decision

words.enDefinition: deep sadness, especially after someone you love dies

examples.en: Even in grief, he kept attending class after his grandfather passed.
examples.zh: 爷爷去世后，即使沉浸在「悲痛」中，他仍坚持上课。

examples.en: Losing her childhood dog brought unexpected grief during finals week.
examples.zh: 期末周里，相伴多年的小狗离世让她陷入「悲伤」。

words.enDefinition: the feeling that everything is wrong and nothing will improve

examples.en: A moment of despair hit me when my laptop crashed before finals.
examples.zh: 期末前电脑崩溃的那一刻，我感到一阵「绝望」。

examples.en: She almost gave up in despair before the scholarship office called.
examples.zh: 奖学金办公室来电之前，她几乎「绝望」得想放弃。

words.enDefinition: the sad feeling of being alone without friends around

examples.en: In a foreign country, loneliness hits hardest on Sunday evenings.
examples.zh: 在国外，周日傍晚的「孤独感」最强烈。

examples.en: Joining the campus photography club finally cured her first-year loneliness.
examples.zh: 加入校园摄影社终于治好了她大一的「孤独感」。

words.enDefinition: the sad feeling of missing your home country and family

examples.en: For international students, homesickness usually peaks around Lunar New Year.
examples.zh: 对我们留学生来说，「乡愁」通常在农历新年前后最浓。

examples.en: Cooking my mom's dumplings is my favorite cure for homesickness.
examples.zh: 照着妈妈的方法包饺子，是我治「想家」的最好办法。

words.enDefinition: a warm, wistful feeling remembering good times in the past

examples.en: A wave of nostalgia hit me when I heard my childhood cartoon song.
examples.zh: 听到童年的动画片主题曲，一阵「怀旧之情」涌上心头。

examples.en: My roommate cooks her grandma's recipes out of pure nostalgia.
examples.zh: 室友做外婆的拿手菜，纯粹是出于「怀念」。

words.enDefinition: the feeling of being very happy about something coming

examples.en: The whole dorm was buzzing with excitement on move-in day.
examples.zh: 搬入日那天，整栋宿舍楼都洋溢着「兴奋」。

examples.en: I could barely sleep because of my excitement about the trip.
examples.zh: 因为对这次旅行太「激动」，我几乎睡不着。

words.enDefinition: the reason or drive that makes you want to act

examples.en: Coffee and deadlines are basically my only motivation during finals.
examples.zh: 咖啡和截止日期基本是我期末唯一的「动力」。

examples.en: Watching senior students succeed gives me motivation to keep studying.
examples.zh: 看到学长学姐们成功，我有了继续努力的「动力」。

words.enDefinition: the feeling of being thankful to someone for kindness

examples.en: I wrote a thank-you card to express my gratitude to my advisor.
examples.zh: 我写了张感谢卡，向导师表达「感激之情」。

examples.en: She cooked dinner for her tutor out of pure gratitude.
examples.zh: 她为导师做了一顿晚饭，聊表「感激」。

words.enDefinition: the feeling of being sorry for someone with problems

examples.en: I have a lot of sympathy for first-year students during finals.
examples.zh: 我很「同情」期末周里的大一新生。

examples.en: He sent flowers as a gesture of sympathy after her loss.
examples.zh: 她遭遇不幸后，他送上鲜花以表「慰问」。

words.enDefinition: the ability to imagine how another person feels

examples.en: Living abroad has taught me real empathy for other cultures.
examples.zh: 在国外生活教会了我对不同文化的「同理心」。

examples.en: Good peer mentors show empathy when freshmen struggle with homesickness.
examples.zh: 新生想家时，优秀的朋辈导师会展现「同理心」。

words.enDefinition: the tendency to become angry suddenly or easily

examples.en: My roommate has a short temper before her morning coffee.
examples.zh: 室友早上没喝到咖啡前，「脾气」很差。

examples.en: I lost my temper when the printer ate my homework again.
examples.zh: 打印机又吞了我的作业，我忍不住「发火」了。

words.enDefinition: the way you feel at a particular time

examples.en: Bad weather puts me in a lazy mood all day.
examples.zh: 坏天气让我一整天都是懒洋洋的「心情」。

examples.en: She's in a great mood after passing her driving test.
examples.zh: 通过驾照考试后，她「心情」大好。

words.enDefinition: the general feeling a place or person gives you, informal

examples.en: This café has such cozy vibes that I study here daily.
examples.zh: 这家咖啡馆「氛围感」超好，我每天都来学习。

examples.en: I got weird vibes from that guy at the welcome party.
examples.zh: 迎新会上那个男生给我的「感觉」怪怪的。

words.enDefinition: the emotions you have about a person or situation

examples.en: It's healthy to talk about your feelings with close friends.
examples.zh: 和亲近的朋友聊聊自己的「内心感受」很健康。

examples.en: My careless comment at dinner that night really hurt her feelings.
examples.zh: 那晚饭桌上我随口一句话，真的「伤了她的感情」。

words.enDefinition: to become happier, or to make someone happier

examples.en: Come on, cheer up! Results come out Friday, and you studied hard.
examples.zh: 「开心点」啦！周五就出成绩了，你复习得那么努力。

examples.en: She brought me milk tea to cheer me up after the exam.
examples.zh: 考试结束后，她给我带奶茶「哄我开心」。

collocations: a little something to cheer you up

words.enDefinition: to become relaxed after being angry or excited

examples.en: Take a deep breath and calm down before you reply to that email.
examples.zh: 深呼吸「冷静」下来，再去回复那封邮件。

examples.en: He finally calmed down after walking around the block twice.
examples.zh: 在外面绕了两圈之后，他终于「平静」下来。

words.enDefinition: to relax and stop being angry or nervous, informal

examples.en: Hey, chill out; one late assignment won't ruin your GPA.
examples.zh: 「放松点」哥们，一次迟交作业不会毁掉你的绩点。

examples.en: We chilled out on the quad after our last exam.
examples.zh: 考完最后一科，我们在中央草坪上「放松」了一会儿。

words.enDefinition: to suddenly lose control of yourself from fear or worry

examples.en: I freaked out when I couldn't find my passport this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上发现护照不见了，我简直「抓狂」了。

examples.en: Don't freak out, but the final exam schedule just changed.
examples.zh: 先别「抓狂」，期末考试安排刚刚有变动。

words.enDefinition: to suddenly feel so worried that you cannot think calmly

examples.en: I started to panic when I couldn't log into the exam portal.
examples.zh: 登不进考试系统时，我开始「慌了」。

examples.en: Try not to panic; the library has spare laptop chargers.
examples.zh: 别「惊慌」，图书馆有备用的笔记本充电器。

words.enDefinition: to release angry feelings by talking about them

examples.en: I called my sister just to vent about my group project.
examples.zh: 我给姐姐打电话，就是为了「吐槽」小组作业。

examples.en: She vented about her noisy neighbors while we ate late-night hotpot.
examples.zh: 吃深夜火锅时，她「大吐苦水」，抱怨吵闹的邻居。

words.enDefinition: to relax after a period of work or tension

examples.en: I unwind by watching cooking videos after long study days.
examples.zh: 长时间学习之后，我靠看美食视频「放松」。

examples.en: A hot shower helps me unwind before bed after my shift.
examples.zh: 下班后洗个热水澡，帮我睡前「放松身心」。

words.enDefinition: to rest so that your energy and good mood return

examples.en: I spent the whole weekend offline to recharge before finals.
examples.zh: 期末前我整个周末都不上网，好好「充电」。

examples.en: A short nap at the library recharges me between classes.
examples.zh: 课间在图书馆小睡一会儿，帮我「恢复精力」。

words.enDefinition: to deal with a difficult situation well enough

examples.en: Keeping a journal really helps me cope with deadline stress.
examples.zh: 写日记确实帮我「应对」截止日期带来的压力。

examples.en: How do you cope with homesickness during such a long semester?
examples.zh: 学期这么长，你是怎么「应对」想家情绪的？

words.enDefinition: to start feeling better after something bad happens

examples.en: It took me a month to get over the failed interview.
examples.zh: 我花了一个月才从那次失败的面试中「走出来」。

examples.en: She still hasn't gotten over missing her own graduation ceremony.
examples.zh: 错过自己的毕业典礼，她至今还没「缓过来」。

words.enDefinition: to stop thinking about something unpleasant and continue life

examples.en: It's time to move on and focus on next semester's goals.
examples.zh: 是时候「向前看」，专注下学期的目标了。

examples.en: He moved on quickly after the club rejected his proposal.
examples.zh: 社团否了他的提案后，他很快「放下」并继续前行。

words.enDefinition: to start talking honestly about your private feelings

examples.en: My roommate slowly opened up about her anxiety during midterms.
examples.zh: 期中考试期间，室友慢慢「敞开心扉」，聊起她的焦虑。

examples.en: He finds it hard to open up to people he just met.
examples.zh: 他很难向刚认识的人「敞开心扉」。

words.enDefinition: to hide your feelings instead of expressing them

examples.en: Don't bottle up your stress; talk to someone you trust.
examples.zh: 别把压力「憋在心里」，找信任的人聊聊。

examples.en: She bottled up her frustration until it exploded at dinner.
examples.zh: 她一直「压抑着」不满，直到晚餐时才爆发。

words.enDefinition: to suddenly start crying or lose emotional control

examples.en: I broke down during the call home and couldn't stop crying.
examples.zh: 打回家的电话时我「情绪崩溃」，哭个不停。

examples.en: She completely broke down after reading her grandfather's old letter.
examples.zh: 读完爷爷的旧信，她彻底「绷不住了」。

words.enDefinition: to suddenly begin crying

examples.en: She burst into tears when the acceptance letter finally arrived.
examples.zh: 录取信终于寄到时，她「一下子哭了出来」。

examples.en: I burst into tears the moment my mom landed at the airport.
examples.zh: 妈妈在机场落地的那一刻，我「放声大哭」。

words.enDefinition: to make someone feel better when they are sad

examples.en: My roommate comforted me after I failed my first midterm.
examples.zh: 第一次期中考砸后，室友「安慰」了我。

examples.en: She comforted her homesick friend with a plate of homemade dumplings.
examples.zh: 她用一盘手工饺子「安慰」想家的朋友。

words.enDefinition: to feel sad because someone or something is absent

examples.en: I really miss my mom's cooking during stressful exam weeks.
examples.zh: 压力大的考试周里，我特别「想念」妈妈做的菜。

examples.en: He missed his hometown friends so much that he flew back.
examples.zh: 他太「想念」家乡的朋友了，干脆飞了回去。

words.enDefinition: to feel worried about something that is going to happen

examples.en: I always dread checking my grades after a difficult exam.
examples.zh: 考完难题之后，我总是「害怕」去查成绩。

examples.en: She dreaded telling her parents about the extra tuition fees.
examples.zh: 她一直「害怕」把额外学费的事告诉父母。

words.enDefinition: to feel excited and happy about something coming

examples.en: I'm really looking forward to our winter break family reunion.
examples.zh: 我特别「期盼」寒假的家庭团聚。

examples.en: She looks forward to her weekly video call with grandma.
examples.zh: 她每周都「盼着」和奶奶视频通话。

collocations: look forward to hearing from you

words.enDefinition: to accept an unpleasant situation without complaining

examples.en: I can't put up with my roommate's 2 a.m. alarm anymore.
examples.zh: 我再也「受不了」室友凌晨两点的闹钟了。

examples.en: We've put up with the construction noise all semester long.
examples.zh: 整个学期我们都在「忍受」施工的噪音。

words.enDefinition: to suddenly speak angrily and sharply to someone

examples.en: Sorry I snapped at you; exam week has me exhausted.
examples.zh: 抱歉刚才「冲你发火」，考试周把我累坏了。

examples.en: She snapped at her brother for borrowing her notes again.
examples.zh: 弟弟又拿她的笔记，她「没好气地吼」了他一句。

words.enDefinition: to keep thinking too much about something bad

examples.en: Try not to dwell on one bad grade for too long.
examples.zh: 别在一门糟糕的成绩上「纠结」太久。

examples.en: He dwelled on the rejection for weeks before moving forward.
examples.zh: 被拒后的几周里他一直「耿耿于怀」，之后才重新出发。

words.enDefinition: to become friendly again after an argument

examples.en: My roommate and I made up the same night we argued.
examples.zh: 我和室友吵架当晚就「和好」了。

examples.en: They argue over chores, but they always make up within a day.
examples.zh: 他们常为家务吵架，但总会在一天内「和好」。

words.enDefinition: to contact someone to see how they are doing

examples.en: My mom checks in on me every Sunday evening by video call.
examples.zh: 妈妈每周日晚上都会视频「问候」我。

examples.en: RAs check in on freshmen during their first few lonely weeks.
examples.zh: 宿管助理会在新生最孤单的头几周「关心探望」他们。

words.enDefinition: to contact someone for help or emotional support

examples.en: Please reach out if coursework ever starts to overwhelm you.
examples.zh: 如果课业让你喘不过气，请随时「向我求助」。

examples.en: She reached out to the counseling center during finals week.
examples.zh: 期末周她主动「联系」了心理咨询中心。

words.enDefinition: to annoy someone again and again

examples.en: My roommate's late-night gaming really gets on my nerves during finals.
examples.zh: 期末期间，室友深夜打游戏真让我「心烦」。

examples.en: The constant beeping of the microwave got on everyone's nerves.
examples.zh: 微波炉不停的哔哔声让大家都「烦躁不已」。

collocations: starting to get on my nerves

words.enDefinition: to stay calm and not get angry

examples.en: Try to keep your cool when the professor questions your citations.
examples.zh: 教授质疑你的引用时，尽量「保持冷静」。

examples.en: He somehow kept his cool during the heated group meeting.
examples.zh: 激烈的组会上，他居然「稳住了情绪」。

words.enDefinition: to control your emotions and act normally again

examples.en: Hey, pull yourself together; you still have two finals to go.
examples.zh: 「振作起来」，你还有两门期末要考。

examples.en: She took a deep breath and pulled herself together before the interview.
examples.zh: 面试前她深吸一口气，「稳住了自己」。

words.enDefinition: to relax and stop pushing yourself so hard

examples.en: You should take it easy this weekend; you've studied enough.
examples.zh: 这周末「放轻松」，现阶段你复习得够多了。

examples.en: The doctor told me to take it easy after the flu.
examples.zh: 流感之后，医生叮嘱我「放轻松」，别太累。

collocations: take it easy for a while
told me to take it easy

words.enDefinition: to stop worrying for a while, often by walking

examples.en: A short walk around campus helps me clear my head.
examples.zh: 在校园里散散步帮我「理清思绪」。

examples.en: Go clear your head; you've stared at that essay for hours.
examples.zh: 去「放空一下脑子」吧，那篇论文你都盯了几个小时了。

collocations: go for a walk to clear your head

words.enDefinition: to help you stop thinking about something worrying

examples.en: Our Friday board game nights take my mind off upcoming deadlines.
examples.zh: 周五的桌游之夜让我「暂时忘掉」临近的截止日期。

examples.en: Cooking takes her mind off the stress of job hunting.
examples.zh: 做饭能让她「不去想」找工作的压力。

collocations: a good way to take your mind off

words.enDefinition: to release anger or stress through energetic activity

examples.en: I play pickup basketball to blow off steam after exams.
examples.zh: 考完试我会去打半场篮球「发泄一下」。

examples.en: She blows off steam by singing loudly in the shower.
examples.zh: 她靠在淋浴时大声唱歌来「释放压力」。

collocations: blow off steam at the gym

words.enDefinition: partly happy and partly unhappy about the same thing

examples.en: I have mixed feelings about graduating and leaving this city.
examples.zh: 对于毕业离开这座城市，我「心情复杂」。

examples.en: She had mixed feelings about her best friend moving closer.
examples.zh: 最好的朋友搬得更近了，她反倒「百感交集」。

words.enDefinition: sudden frequent changes between happy and unhappy moods

examples.en: Finals always give me mood swings between panic and hope.
examples.zh: 期末总让我「情绪波动」，一会儿恐慌一会儿充满希望。

examples.en: Her dramatic mood swings during exam week worried her roommate.
examples.zh: 考试周她「情绪起伏」太大，让室友很担心。

words.enDefinition: a short encouraging talk that makes you feel confident

examples.en: My dad gave me a pep talk before my scholarship interview.
examples.zh: 奖学金面试前，爸爸给我「加油打气」。

examples.en: Our captain's five-minute pep talk lifted the whole team's spirits.
examples.zh: 队长五分钟的「动员」让全队士气大振。

words.enDefinition: worried that something that is about to happen may go badly

examples.en: I felt apprehensive about speaking first at the welcome session for new students.
examples.zh: 要在新生欢迎会上第一个发言，我「心里有些忐忑」。

examples.en: My roommate looked apprehensive as we waited outside the unfamiliar lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我们在陌生的讲堂外等候时，室友看起来「心里有些忐忑」。

words.enDefinition: suddenly surprised and momentarily unsure how to respond

examples.en: I was taken aback when the tutor invited me to lead the discussion.
examples.zh: 导师请我主持讨论时，我「愣了一下」。

examples.en: My friend seemed taken aback by the question about her hometown.
examples.zh: 朋友听到关于她老家的问题时，好像「愣了一下」。

collocations: be taken aback by a question

words.enDefinition: to feel that you do not fit or belong in a particular situation

examples.en: I began to feel out of place when everyone else knew one another.
examples.zh: 其他人都互相认识，我开始「感觉自己格格不入」。

examples.en: I used to feel out of place at large events on campus.
examples.zh: 我以前参加校内大型活动时，总「感觉自己格格不入」。

collocations: feel out of place at a party
start to feel out of place

words.enDefinition: to have strong reasons or wishes pulling you in two different directions

examples.en: I still feel torn between the local placement and visiting my family in summer.
examples.zh: 我在本地实习和暑假回家探亲之间还是「感觉左右为难」。

examples.en: You can feel torn when two close friends need help at once.
examples.zh: 两个好朋友同时需要帮忙时，可能会「感觉左右为难」。

words.enDefinition: to talk about something that has been worrying you so you feel better

examples.en: Sometimes it helps to get something off your chest by talking to a friend.
examples.zh: 有时跟朋友聊聊，把「心里的烦恼说出来」，会好受些。

examples.en: My friend said it helps to get something off your chest before trying to sleep.
examples.zh: 朋友说，睡觉前「说出心里的烦恼」会好受些。

collocations: need to get something off your chest
want to get something off your chest
take time to get something off your chest

words.enDefinition: a sudden feeling of dread that something bad has happened or will happen

examples.en: I got a sinking feeling when the train stopped far from the station.
examples.zh: 列车在离车站很远的地方停下时，我「心里一沉」。

examples.en: She had a sinking feeling after realizing her bag was still on the bus.
examples.zh: 她意识到包还在公交车上时，「心里一沉」。
